description:
FILED s473t4 (#1501 CHECK 1 round 1, 2026-09-13).  t/op/for.t is TRANSPILE-FAIL: P 148/1, C 0/0 -- the whole file, 149 rows.

    $ ./pl2cl < t/op/for.t
    PCL: cannot parse (inline code): PPI failed to tokenize it

BISECTED to t/op/for.t:767 (smallest failing prefix, by binary search over line prefixes):
    my $f = "a_low_refcnt_package_var";
    my $i = 0;
    no strict 'refs';
    for ${*$f} (5,11,33) {

MINIMAL REPRODUCERS (PPI 1.291, perl 5.40.3) -- the LEXER, not the tokenizer:
    for ${*$f} (5,11,33) { }   => FAIL: Lexer failed: Illegal state in 'for' compound statement
    foreach ${*$f} (1,2) { }   => FAIL: same
    for ${$f} (1,2) { }        => FAIL: same
    for $$f (1,2) { }          => FAIL: same      <-- the smallest form
    my $x = ${*$f};            => OK              <-- the same deref OUTSIDE a for head is fine

So the trigger is exactly "the foreach loop variable is a DEREFERENCE rather than a plain Symbol"; PPI's `for`-compound lexer accepts a Symbol (`for $x (â¦)`) and a `my`-declaration and nothing else.

PERL ACCEPTS ALL OF THEM:
    $ perl -e 'our $z = 7; my $f = "z"; no strict "refs"; my @seen;
               for $$f (5,11) { push @seen, $$f } print "@seen z=$z\n"'
    5 11 z=7
(the loop aliases the SYMBOL-REF target and restores it afterwards -- that is what op/for.t:767 is testing).

LOGGED as docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§29 with a failing row in docs/ppi-bug-report.t (s473t4, same commit as this filing).

WHAT PCL OWES: a token/lex repair of the shape the other Â§-entries use (rewrite the for-head into a shape PPI lexes, then restore the deref when lowering), or the loop-variable grammar in Parser2's `_lower_compound`.  It is a repair, not a filler -- round t5a.

=== SIZED, NOT FIXED (s473t5a, 2026-09-13) ===

MEASURED FIRST, because it changes the shape of the job: **148 of the file's
149 rows are BEFORE the offending line.**  t/op/for.t has 775 lines and 136
assertion call sites up to line 766; line 767 is the `for ${*$f} (5,11,33)`
loop and there is exactly ONE assertion after it (`is($i, 3, "deleting glob is
safe")` at 771) plus `done_testing()`.  So the prize is "make the document
LEX", not "lower a dereferenced loop variable" -- those are separable, and only
the first one is worth 148 rows.

WHAT THE REPAIR MUST BE, and what it cannot be:

* NOT the `_ppi_parse` serialize+reparse family (`_fix_modulo_magic`,
  `_fix_spaced_sigils`, `_desugar_anon_signatures`, …).  Every one of those
  mutates a DOCUMENT and re-serializes it; here `PPI::Document->new` returns
  undef, so there is no document to mutate.  DO NOT RETRY that route.

* NOT a source-TEXT regex either (the #455 rule: the repair is the BOUNDARY,
  not the text) -- a `for` inside a string, a comment or a heredoc would be
  hit.

* The available route is the TOKEN stream: `PPI::Tokenizer->new(\$src)` +
  `get_token` succeeds on this input (it is the LEXER that fails), and the
  tokens rejoin to the source EXACTLY -- measured, `join '', map { $_->content }
  @tok` eq `$src` on t/op/for.t.  So the offsets are derivable from the token
  list and the splice is decided on tokens even though it is applied to text,
  after which `PPI::Document->new` is re-run.  The token shape to look for
  (measured on the reproducer):
      Word[for] Whitespace Cast[$] Structure[{] Cast[*] Symbol[$f] Structure[}]
      Whitespace Structure[(] …
  i.e. a `for`/`foreach` Word followed by a Cast run instead of a Symbol or a
  `my`.

* THE TRIGGER IS FREE: run the repair ONLY when the first
  `PPI::Document->new` returned undef.  Today that is a hard die ("PCL: cannot
  parse … PPI failed to tokenize it"), so the new path is reachable by exactly
  the files that currently produce nothing -- zero risk to every other file,
  and no cost on the normal path.

THE SECOND PIECE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-HOUR FIX.  Making the file lex
without deciding the loop variable is a SILENT WRONG, by reading of
`Pl/Parser2.pm`'s `_lower_compound` for/foreach arm:

    my ($list)  = grep { $_->isa('PPI::Structure::List') }  @k;
    my ($block) = grep { $_->isa('PPI::Structure::Block') } @k;
    my ($var)   = grep { $_->isa('PPI::Token::Symbol') }    @k;
    die "Parser2 TODO: foreach without list" unless $list && $block;
    my $name = $var ? $var->content : '$_';

For `for ${*$f} (LIST) BLOCK` the FIRST `Structure::Block` among the children
is the deref's own `{*$f}`, not the loop body, and there is no direct Symbol
child -- so `$block` would be the wrong block and the loop would alias `$_`.
For the `for $$f (LIST)` spelling `$var` IS found and is `$f`, so the loop
would bind the NAME STRING instead of its referent.  Two distinct silent
wrongs, both from the same missing verdict.

So the honest fix is THREE pieces: (1) the pre-lex token repair, (2) a verdict
for a non-Symbol loop variable in that arm -- and note a bare `die` there costs
the whole file again, so it has to reach the per-statement DROP path
(`Pl/Parser.pm`'s `_dropped_statement_cl` / `_announce_dropped_statement`, which
v2 reaches through the v1 seam), and (3) eventually the real semantics: perl
LOCALIZES the package variable the deref names and ALIASES it to each element,
which needs `p-foreach` to bind a cell designator computed at run time.  PCL
already binds a GLOBAL loop variable, so (3) is "a symbolic cell", not new
machinery -- but it is not free, and a `local`-plus-copy desugaring is NOT
equivalent (no write-through to the element).

RECOMMENDED SPLIT for whoever takes it: (2) first, alone -- it closes a latent
silent-wrong (rule 12) and is 3 lines plus a guard; then (1)+(3) together, with
t/op/for.t as the acceptance file and `is($i, 3, "deleting glob is safe")` as
the one row that proves the aliasing.

The PPI side is logged as `docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md` section 29 (already) and
gained a SIBLING section 29a in s473t5a: `for my \$x (\$y) {…}`, a DECLARED
ref, does not fail the lexer but falls out of the compound -- same
loop-variable slot, milder symptom, task #1649, 195 rows of t/op/decl-refs.t.
subject: PPI 1.291 LEXER fails on a DEREFERENCE as the foreach loop variable (`for $$f (â¦)`, `for ${*$f} (â¦)`) -- "Illegal state in `for` compound statement" loses all 149 rows of op/for.t
